newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas busy for weekend, Q3, otherwise quiet.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas busy for weekend, Q3, otherwise quiet.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market was well traded for the weekend and the third quarter on Friday, traders and brokers said, but was otherwise quiet with prices little changed.
The third quarter saw the biggest volume of trade.

The market opened at around 10.40 pence a therm, with some saying that trade was done as high as 10.45 pence. Prices then slipped through the morning, with talk eventually reaching a level of 10.25 pence a therm.
There were some who said trade had been concluded at this price, although this was unconfirmed.
But prices then started to bounce back, traders said. "It was offered down quite sharply, then when it hit 10.25 offers backed away rapidly, and it came back up to 10.40," a trader said.
The other period of most interest was the weekend, where one major buyer was reported looking for large volumes.

A dealer said the market opened below 10 pence a therm and was quickly offered as high as 10.50 pence on the realisation that a buyer was prepared to move, but there were also deals done at lower levels.
There was some interest in the fourth quarter, done on its own at least twice and as part of a strip with Q1, but interest for other periods was slim.
It was reported but not confirmed that the year from October 1998 was traded at 13.70 pence a therm, in line with prices seen on Thursday. Otherwise the OTC market was quiet.
The IPE futures market was extremely thin and dull, with only two trades totalling 55 lots done all day.

Transco forecast gas consumption for Saturday at 215 mcm, 50 percent of peak day demand. The temperature is expected to reach 6.9 Celsius, well below the seasonal normal 10.00 Celsius, and the cooler weather was seen as one of the reasons behind the price rise in weekend gas.
